papers.title: EsViritu is a sensitive and specific profiler for viral pathogen detection and genome recovery in metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic sequencing allows for detection of any number of pathogenic viruses from a single sample without a priori knowledge of its contents. This has created a substantial opportunity to characterize pathogens in humans and their environment, but the field is held back by a lack of bioinformatics tools for taxonomic profiling and reconstructing virus genomes. The ideal profiler would simultaneously do two things: report viruses at single-read sensitivity so that ultra-low-abundance pathogens are not missed and hold near-perfect specificity so that a pathogen is never falsely reported. Here
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: EsViritu is a new bioinformatics tool for detecting viral pathogens and reconstructing their genomes directly from metagenomic sequencing data. It aims to achieve single-read sensitivity for ultra-low-abundance viruses while maintaining near-perfect specificity to avoid false positives. This addresses a key gap in viral metagenomics profiling tools.

papers.title: Evaluation of Parallel Accumulation-Serial Fragmentation methods for metaproteomics using a model microbiome.
papers.abstract: We present a multi-organism, ground-truth metaproteomic dataset generated using data-dependent acquisition Parallel Accumulation-Serial Fragmentation (ddaPASEF) and data-independent acquisition (diaPASEF) on a trapped ion mobility mass spectrometer. The dataset comprises 28 species (30 strains) spanning Archaea, Bacteria, Eukarya, and bacteriophages, assembled into an uneven mock community with a 400-fold dynamic range of organismal abundance. Four biological replicates were processed using a standardized sample preparation workflow and analyzed using described LC-MS conditions. Raw data, sear
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This study introduces a ground-truth metaproteomic dataset from a mock microbiome of 28 species (30 strains) spanning Archaea, Bacteria, Eukarya, and bacteriophages with a 400-fold dynamic range. The authors compare ddaPASEF and diaPASEF acquisition methods on a trapped ion mobility mass spectrometer across four biological replicates. The dataset provides a benchmark resource for evaluating metaproteomic workflows and quantification accuracy.

papers.title: Genome-resolved ecology and evolution of the microbiome enabled by quantitative long-read metagenomics.
papers.abstract: Standard metagenomics resolves microbial communities only in relative terms and at coarse taxonomic resolution, obscuring how individual strains change in absolute abundance and evolve within a host. We present long-read quantiomics (LRQ), a quantitative metagenomics platform coupling long-read sequencing with plasmid-based internal standards to recover high-quality genomes, including from degraded or low-input stool, and measure absolute, genome-resolved strain abundances. We validate LRQ using large plasmid standards and bacterial spike-ins, then apply it to eight years of dense sampling fro
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors present long-read quantiomics (LRQ), a quantitative metagenomics platform that combines long-read sequencing with plasmid-based internal standards to recover high-quality microbial genomes and measure absolute, strain-resolved abundances. They validate the method using plasmid standards and bacterial spike-ins, then apply it to eight years of dense longitudinal sampling to track how individual strains change in absolute abundance and evolve within a host. This enables genome-resolved ecological and evolutionary analysis of the microbiome, even from degraded or low-input stool samples.

papers.title: Mediation Analysis with Compositional Exposures.
papers.abstract: Understanding the causal pathways linking the gut microbiome to downstream biomarkers and clinical outcomes is central to microbiome research. When the microbiome acts as the exposure, the high dimensionality and compositional structure of the data introduce unique methodological challenges for mediation analysis. To address these challenges, we propose a latent variable mediation framework that captures variation in microbial composition through a microbial balance, defined as the log-ratio between two unknown subsets of taxa. This balance serves as a latent scalar exposure and simplifies the
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors propose a latent variable mediation framework for microbiome studies where the exposure is a high-dimensional compositional microbial community. Their method summarizes microbial variation into a single 'balance' (log-ratio of two unknown taxon subsets) that acts as a latent scalar exposure, simplifying mediation analysis of pathways from the microbiome to downstream biomarkers and clinical outcomes.

papers.title: New genetic tools in Finegoldia magna identify a conserved adhesin required for the formation of stress-tolerant aggregates.
papers.abstract: The Gram-positive obligate anaerobe Finegoldia magna is a member of the healthy human microbiota, but also acts as an opportunistic pathogen to cause persistent, biofilm-associated infections. Despite its prevalence on the human host, little is known about F. magna biology or the mechanisms underlying its clinically relevant phenotypes, partly due to the lack of genetic tools. We address this gap by establishing genetic approaches for investigating gene function in F. magna , which we apply to identify genetic determinants of aggregate biofilm formation. We found that F. magna isolates are nat
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint establishes new genetic tools for the understudied Gram-positive anaerobe Finegoldia magna, a common member of the human microbiota that can also cause persistent biofilm infections. Using these tools, the authors identify a conserved adhesin required for the formation of stress-tolerant aggregates, providing the first genetic handle on clinically relevant biofilm phenotypes in this organism.

papers.title: Sequencing the wastewater virome: Current strategies and bioinformatic pitfalls.
papers.abstract: Wastewater-based surveillance (WBS) is a powerful tool for monitoring viral pathogens at the population level, complementing clinical surveillance through anonymous and unbiased insights into viral circulation. Wastewater sequencing allows to move beyond detection toward detailed characterization of circulating pathogens. This review outlines the two main sequencing strategies used in WBS: targeted and untargeted approaches. Targeted methods, including amplicon- and probe-based sequencing, provide sensitive detection and recovery of known viruses but are limited in identifying novel pathogens.
papers.summary: This review examines sequencing strategies for wastewater-based surveillance of viral pathogens, comparing targeted approaches (amplicon- and probe-based) with untargeted methods. It highlights that targeted methods offer sensitive detection of known viruses but cannot identify novel pathogens, and discusses bioinformatic pitfalls in the field.

papers.title: A global atlas of the gut virome reveals subtype-specific and functional alterations in irritable bowel syndrome.
papers.abstract: The gut virome is a critical component of the microbiome-gut-brain axis; however, its role in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) remains poorly understood due to limited sample sizes and geographic bias. We aimed to construct a comprehensive global atlas of the IBS gut virome to elucidate its composition, functional potential, and clinical relevance across diverse populations and IBS subtypes. We integrated multi-cohort data comprising 1,104 samples (790 IBS patients and 314 healthy controls) from 11 cohorts across 10 geographic regions. A standardized bioinformatic pipeline was employed to perfor
papers.summary: This study integrates gut virome data from 1,104 samples across 11 cohorts and 10 geographic regions to build a global atlas of the gut virome in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). The authors identify subtype-specific virome alterations and functional changes associated with IBS, providing a comprehensive resource for understanding the virome's role in the microbiome-gut-brain axis. The work highlights the importance of diverse populations in uncovering IBS-related viral signatures.

papers.title: Association of quantitative sputum Candida load with respiratory dysbiosis and airway inflammation in suspected invasive pulmonary candidiasis.
papers.abstract: The clinical significance of Candida species isolation from sputum remains ambiguous due to the colonization-infection dilemma. Integrating quantitative culture with microbiome profiling may clarify its role, yet systematic evidence is scarce. In this exploratory study (June 2023-June 2026), we enrolled 140 hospitalized patients suspected of invasive pulmonary candidiasis (IPC) and stratified them into possible IPC (n = 36), probable IPC (n = 71), and negative control (n = 33) groups based on clinical criteria. All underwent quantitative fungal culture of sputum and metagenomic next-generation
papers.summary: This exploratory study of 140 hospitalized patients suspected of invasive pulmonary candidiasis combined quantitative sputum fungal culture with metagenomic sequencing to examine whether Candida burden relates to respiratory microbiome disruption and airway inflammation. The authors stratified patients into possible, probable, and negative IPC groups, aiming to clarify whether sputum Candida isolation reflects true infection versus colonization. The findings suggest that quantitative Candida load associates with respiratory dysbiosis and inflammation, potentially helping distinguish infection from colonization.

papers.title: Breastfeeding and maternal microbial reservoirs are associated with infant gut phageome development during the first year of life.
papers.abstract: The early-life assembly of the gut microbiome is a critical determinant of long-term health, yet the role of bacteriophages in this process remains poorly understood. Here we longitudinally profile the gut phageome of 34 mother-infant dyads during the first year of life with metagenomics and a phage-centered computational workflow. Phage diversity increases with age, paralleling bacterial diversification but following distinct ecological trajectories. Shared viral populations across maternal and infant samples are consistent with potential maternal contribution, although not indicative of dire
papers.summary: This study longitudinally tracked the gut phageome of 34 mother-infant pairs over the first year of life using metagenomics and a phage-focused computational pipeline. Phage diversity increased with infant age, mirroring bacterial diversification but following distinct ecological patterns, and shared viral populations between mothers and infants suggest potential maternal transmission of phages. The findings highlight breastfeeding and maternal microbial reservoirs as factors shaping early infant gut phageome development.

papers.title: Effects of probiotics on joint homeostasis and osteoarthritis: Development of microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip.
papers.abstract: Although emerging evidence implicates gut microbiome-cartilage cross-talk in the pathogenesis of osteoarthritis (OA), the most common joint disease, studying this microbe-gut-joint axis remains challenging due to limitations of animal models and conventional in vitro systems. Here, we report a microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip (MGCAoC) that recreates tissue-specific microenvironments with oxygen gradients and physiological fluid shear. The computer simulation-optimized chip design generates an anoxic-oxic interface for the gut module and enables perfusion of probiotic metabolites to human c
papers.summary: Researchers developed a microbe-gut-cartilage axis-on-a-chip (MGCAoC) that mimics the oxygen gradients and fluid shear of the gut-joint environment, allowing study of how gut microbes and their metabolites influence cartilage health. The chip enables perfusion of probiotic metabolites to human cartilage cells, providing a new platform to investigate the gut microbiome's role in osteoarthritis pathogenesis.

papers.title: Obtaining maximum information from colony counts with REPOP.
papers.abstract: Bacterial counts from native environments, such as soil or the animal gut, often show substantial variability across replicate samples. This heterogeneity is typically attributed to genetic or environmental factors. A common approach to estimating bacterial populations involves successive dilution and plating, followed by multiplying colony counts by dilution factors. This method, however, overestimates the heterogeneity in bacterial population because it conflates the inherent uncertainty in drawing a subsample from the total population with the uncertainty in the sample arising from biologic
papers.summary: The paper introduces REPOP, a statistical method for analyzing colony counts from dilution plating experiments. It addresses the common problem that multiplying colony counts by dilution factors overestimates biological heterogeneity by conflating sampling noise with true biological variability. REPOP aims to extract more accurate estimates of bacterial population sizes and their variability from standard colony count data.

papers.title: Deciphering the heterogeneity of prodromal α-synucleinopathy: linking brain biotyping and gut dysbiosis in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated/idiopathic REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) is a specific prodrome of α-synucleinopathies. We previously identified two distinct clinical-neuroimaging biotypes in iRBD: Biotype 1, marked by widespread cortical-subcortical-cerebellar atrophy with motor and cognitive deficits, and Biotype 2, with preserved brain structure and neurocognition. Converging evidence implicates the gut-brain axis in early α-synucleinopathy, yet its role in these divergent iRBD phenotypes remains unexplored.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether the two previously identified brain biotypes of isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD) — one with widespread brain atrophy and cognitive/motor deficits, the other with preserved brain structure — differ in their gut microbiome composition. By linking brain biotyping with gut dysbiosis, the authors aim to clarify how the gut-brain axis contributes to the heterogeneous prodromal stages of α-synucleinopathies like Parkinson's disease.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics and metabolic modeling links structure to function in high-performing electrosynthetic biofilm communities.
papers.abstract: Microbial electrosynthesis (MES) is a promising technology for the valorization of CO2 into industrially relevant building blocks. The high-performing MES systems in terms of production rates of acetate (12.5-19.7 mmol L-1catholyte day-1), butyrate (1.9-12.2 mmol L-1catholyte day-1), and caproate (0.6-0.9 mmol L-1catholyte day-1) discussed in this study consist of mixed microbial communities. However, the microbial community members, metabolic pathways, and interactions driving product formation in MES communities remain poorly understood. To overcome these challenges, we conducted a comprehen
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with metabolic modeling to characterize the microbial community members and metabolic pathways responsible for high-rate production of acetate, butyrate, and caproate in electrosynthetic biofilms. The work links community structure to metabolic function, providing mechanistic insight into how mixed microbial consortia drive CO2 valorization in microbial electrosynthesis systems.

papers.title: Novel Antarctic chemolithotroph drives iron biomineralization.
papers.abstract: Iron, the most abundant redox-active metal in the Earth's crust, is coupled to numerous biogeochemical cycles. However, the mechanisms of iron oxidation and the organisms involved remain incompletely understood. Banded iron formations (BIFs) are a major reservoir of iron ore in the Precambrian sedimentary record, yet the biological contribution to their genesis remains a subject of unresolved debate. While large-scale BIF deposition largely ceased after the Proterozoic, microbial activity in modern Holocene sediments under fluctuating redox conditions provides a unique opportunity to examine m
papers.summary: This study characterizes a novel Antarctic chemolithotrophic microorganism that drives iron biomineralization, providing direct evidence for microbial iron oxidation in modern sedimentary environments. The findings offer a modern analog for understanding the biological contribution to ancient banded iron formations (BIFs), a long-debated question in Precambrian geology.

papers.title: [Translated article] The "Trojan horse" against antimicrobial resistance: Siderophore conjugates and public health.
papers.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance, particularly in carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales such as KPC-type, represents a critical threat to public health in Latin America, associated with high mortality rates and increased healthcare costs. This systematic review aims to evaluate the therapeutic potential of siderophore-drug and siderophore-peptide conjugates against priority multidrug-resistant pathogens, including Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii, analyzing their efficacy, mechanisms of action, and implementation challenges.
papers.journal: Farmacia hospitalaria : organo oficial de expresion cientifica de la Sociedad Espanola de Farmacia Hospitalaria
papers.summary: This systematic review evaluates siderophore-drug and siderophore-peptide conjugates as a 'Trojan horse' strategy to combat multidrug-resistant pathogens like carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and Acinetobacter baumannii. It analyzes their efficacy, mechanisms of action, and barriers to clinical implementation, with a focus on the public health burden in Latin America.

papers.title: Escherichia coli-derived enterobactin is associated with delayed gut microbiome maturation in infants born to mothers with obesity.
papers.abstract: Maternal obesity has been increasingly recognized as a factor influencing early-life microbiome development. However, its impact on the infant gut resistome and virulome remains insufficiently characterized. In this prospective longitudinal study, we investigated gut microbiome composition, antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), and virulence factor profiles in infants born to mothers with obesity and normal weight during the first year of life. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed on maternal and infant fecal samples collected at birth and at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. Infants born to obese
papers.summary: This prospective longitudinal study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to track gut microbiome composition, antibiotic resistance genes, and virulence factors in infants born to mothers with obesity versus normal weight over the first year of life. The authors found that Escherichia coli-derived enterobactin, a siderophore, was associated with delayed gut microbiome maturation in infants of mothers with obesity. The work links maternal obesity to altered early-life microbiome development and the infant resistome/virulome.

papers.title: A joint mixture Tobit method with latent microbial abundance improves detection of microbiome-disease associations in zero-inflated data.
papers.abstract: Zero inflation remains a major challenge in microbiome differential abundance analysis, often resulting in inflated type I error rates or reduced statistical power. Although numerous methods have been proposed to address excess zeros, many existing approaches do not explicitly distinguish between distinct zero-generating mechanisms, and censoring-based modeling perspectives remain relatively underexplored in microbiome data analysis. To advance methodological development in this area, we introduce a novel censoring-based modeling perspective for microbiome differential abundance analysis. Spec
papers.summary: The paper introduces a joint mixture Tobit model that treats zero-inflated microbiome counts as censored observations of a latent microbial abundance, explicitly separating biological zeros from technical zeros. This censoring-based approach improves detection of microbiome-disease associations by controlling type I error and increasing power compared to existing differential abundance methods.

papers.title: Peripheral microbial metabolites as indicators of gut microbiome disruption: systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiome disruption is often characterized by the loss of obligately anaerobic bacteria, which may lead to altered production of microbial metabolites that can be detected peripherally. The application of widely used sequencing-based microbiome analyses to clinical settings is limited by cost, turnaround time, and challenges with patients with very low stool output. Since some products of strictly bacterial metabolism are detectable in blood, peripheral metabolites may provide a rapid and scalable indicator of gut microbiome composition and function. We performed a systematic review and
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis examines whether microbial metabolites detectable in blood can serve as indicators of gut microbiome disruption, which is typically marked by loss of obligate anaerobes. The authors synthesize evidence on peripheral metabolite signatures as a rapid, scalable alternative to sequencing-based microbiome analysis, which is limited by cost, turnaround time, and low stool output in some patients.

papers.title: Mallard super-shedders of avian influenza exhibit distinct cloacal microbial abundance profiles.
papers.abstract: In many infectious disease systems, a small fraction of hosts accounts for a disproportionate share of transmission, but the biological basis of this heterogeneity remains poorly resolved. In avian influenza, mallards show substantial variation in viral shedding, raising the possibility that only a subset of individuals contributes strongly to environmental contamination and onward spread. To examine whether host microbiome structure is associated with this variation, we experimentally infected wild, captive mallards with low-pathogenic avian influenza virus. We characterized cloacal microbiom
papers.summary: This study experimentally infected captive wild mallards with low-pathogenic avian influenza and found that individuals with the highest viral shedding (super-shedders) had distinct cloacal microbiome abundance profiles compared to low shedders. The results suggest that host microbiome composition may contribute to heterogeneity in influenza transmission.

papers.title: Chestnut-quebracho tannins shape the fecal metabolome of weaned pigs through microbiota-dependent urolithin production.
papers.abstract: Chestnut and quebracho tannins may support gut health in weaned piglets, but their efficacy likely depends on farm environment and microbial capacity to convert tannins into bioactive metabolites. This study evaluated the effects of a blend of chestnut-derived hydrolysable tannins and quebracho-derived condensed tannins on growth performance, diarrhea occurrence, gut metagenome, and fecal metabolome in piglets reared under two commercial farm conditions. A total of 160 weaned piglets (initial body weight 6.53 ± 0.13 kg) were assigned to a 2 × 2 factorial design comprising 2 weaning units (W1 a
papers.journal: Journal of animal science and biotechnology
papers.summary: This study tested whether a blend of chestnut (hydrolysable) and quebracho (condensed) tannins improves gut health in weaned piglets across two commercial farm environments. Tannin supplementation shaped the fecal metabolome primarily through microbiota-dependent conversion of tannins into bioactive urolithins, with effects varying by farm condition. The findings suggest that tannin efficacy depends on the piglets' microbial capacity to metabolize these compounds.

papers.title: Leviathan: fast, memory-efficient, and scalable taxonomic and pathway profiling for (pan)genome-resolved metagenomics and metatranscriptomics.
papers.abstract: Functional profiling of meta-omics is essential for understanding microbial communities, yet support for custom genome-resolved reference databases is limited. We introduce Leviathan for integrated taxonomic and functional profiling at both genome and pangenome resolution. Leviathan combines Sylph for ultrafast alignment-free taxonomic profiling with Salmon for pseudo-alignment-based read quantification in DNA space against (pan)genome-resolved gene catalogs, producing dual metrics per (pan)genome: pathway abundance and graph-based pathway coverage. Benchmarking alignment backends on synthetic
papers.summary: Leviathan is a new tool that combines fast alignment-free taxonomic profiling (Sylph) with pseudo-alignment-based gene quantification (Salmon) to enable integrated taxonomic and functional profiling of metagenomes and metatranscriptomes against custom genome- and pangenome-resolved reference databases. It produces per-genome pathway abundance and graph-based pathway coverage metrics, addressing the limited support for custom reference databases in existing functional profiling tools.

papers.title: PanGBank: a large-scale resource of precomputed microbial pangenomes built with PPanGGOLiN.
papers.abstract: PanGBank (https://pangbank.genoscope.cns.fr) is a comprehensive open-access database providing precomputed prokaryotic pangenomes at a broad taxonomic scale. Built upon PPanGGOLiN partitioned pangenome graphs, PanGBank addresses the growing need for large-scale comparative genomics through a standardized, regularly updated, and fully accessible resource. The initial release comprises two complementary collections covering >4600 prokaryotic species from the Genome Taxonomy Database (GTDB), encompassing over 393 000 genomes: GTDB_all, maximizing taxonomic and environmental diversity through the
papers.summary: PanGBank is a new open-access database offering precomputed pangenomes for over 4,600 prokaryotic species (393,000+ genomes), built using the PPanGGOLiN partitioned pangenome graph method. It provides a standardized, regularly updated resource that removes the computational burden of generating pangenomes for large-scale comparative genomics. The initial release includes two collections (GTDB_all and another) covering broad taxonomic and environmental diversity.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of rhizosphere soil microbiota in wild and cultivated Notopterygium incisum, an umbelliferae medicinal herb.
papers.abstract: Notopterygium incisum is not only a traditional Chinese medicine but also an endemic herb. Artificial domestication and large-scale cultivation are crucial for resolving the crisis of wild resources and the supply-demand imbalance of N. incisum, yet current techniques have failed to stably provide the herb medicine in good quality. Metagenomic analyses revealed significant differences in the rhizomicrobiota between wild and cultivated N. incisum, particularly in microbial composition, gene functions, and community assembly. The rhizomicrobiota of the wild N. incisum from 3 different sites with
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic sequencing to compare the rhizosphere soil microbiota of wild versus cultivated Notopterygium incisum, a medicinal herb from the Umbelliferae family. The authors found significant differences in microbial composition, gene functions, and community assembly between wild and cultivated plants, suggesting that domestication alters the root-associated microbiome. These findings may help explain why cultivated herbs often fail to match the quality of wild ones.

papers.title: Comparative evaluation of methods for measuring standardized ileal digestibility of amino acids for different sorghum varieties in broilers.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the effects of two evaluation methods (direct vs. substitution) on standardized ileal amino acid digestibility (SIDAA) and intestinal digestive physiology in broilers fed sorghum from six regional sources. There were 336 27-d-old Cobb broilers assigned to 14 treatments, including a nitrogen-free diet (NFD), a corn-soybean meal (CSM) basal diet, and 12 experimental diets arranged in a 2 × 6 factorial arrangement. In the direct method, sorghum served as the only source of dietary amino acids whereas in substitution method the test sorghum replaced 40% (w/w) of the basal d
papers.summary: This study compared direct and substitution methods for measuring standardized ileal amino acid digestibility (SIDAA) in broilers fed sorghum from six regional sources. Using 336 Cobb broilers across 14 dietary treatments, the authors evaluated how the two methods affect digestibility estimates and intestinal digestive physiology. The findings provide guidance on method selection for accurate amino acid digestibility assessment in poultry nutrition.

papers.title: Salivary microbiome responses to chlorhexidine and Coriandrum sativum essential oil mouthwashes in patients with periodontitis in a randomized 2-week clinical trial.
papers.abstract: To compare the short-term salivary microbiome effects of a Coriandrum sativum essential oil (CSEO) mouthwash, chlorhexidine (CHX) as a benchmark comparator, and water in patients with periodontitis.
papers.summary: This randomized 2-week clinical trial compared the salivary microbiome effects of a Coriandrum sativum essential oil mouthwash, chlorhexidine, and water in periodontitis patients. The study characterizes how these mouthwashes shift the oral microbial community, providing short-term evidence on the microbiome impact of a natural alternative to chlorhexidine.

papers.title: Subclinical Mastitis and Antibiotic Exposure Reshape the Milk Bacteriome, Resistome, and Metabolic Functional Profiles in Dairy Cows.
papers.abstract: Subclinical mastitis (SCM) reduces milk yield and promotes antibiotic use, contributing to antimicrobial resistance. However, information on milk microbiome dysbiosis and resistome alterations in dairy cows remains limited. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 30 milk samples from 20 cows classified as SCM (n = 10), antibiotic-treated (ANT; n = 10), and healthy milk (HM; n = 10). Bacteriome, resistome, and metabolic functions were analyzed using bioinformatic tools. Microbial alpha diversity was significantly higher in HM than SCM and ANT samples (p < 0.05), with the greatest richnes
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing of milk samples from dairy cows to compare the bacteriome, resistome, and metabolic functional profiles between subclinical mastitis (SCM), antibiotic-treated (ANT), and healthy milk (HM). Healthy milk showed significantly higher microbial alpha diversity than SCM and ANT samples, indicating that both subclinical mastitis and antibiotic exposure disrupt the milk microbiome and its functional potential, including antimicrobial resistance genes.

papers.title: Genotype-dependent phosphorus acquisition responses of two soybean genotypes under combined low phosphorus and salt stress: evidence from root traits, exudates and rhizosphere microbiome.
papers.abstract: Soil salinization and phosphorus (P) deficiency often co-occur in coastal saline-alkali soils, severely limiting crop productivity. Although root exudates are known to mediate rhizosphere microbiome assembly, the coordinated associations among root exudates, rhizosphere microbes, and P acquisition under combined salinity stress and phosphate deficiency remain unclear. In this study, we used two salt-tolerant soybean genotypes differing in P efficiency (A74, P-efficient; A6, P-inefficient) as materials. In a controlled pot experiment, four treatments were established: control (CK), low P (LP),
papers.summary: This study examined how two soybean genotypes with differing phosphorus efficiency respond to combined low phosphorus and salt stress, focusing on root traits, root exudates, and rhizosphere microbiome composition. The P-efficient genotype (A74) showed distinct root and exudate responses that were associated with beneficial rhizosphere microbial recruitment, suggesting genotype-dependent strategies for phosphorus acquisition under saline-low-P conditions.

papers.title: Association of microbial pathways predicted/inferred using 16S and shotgun metagenome with faecal metabolite abundances.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiome is an essential metabolic organ influencing host health through metabolite production. While metabolite production levels can be directly measured by gas or liquid chromatography, they are commonly inferred from the abundance of metagenomic functional pathways. To evaluate the accuracy of these inferences, we established a single, manually curated metabolite-pathway/enzyme mapping list as a standardized biological reference. We then compared liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based faecal metabolites with functional pathways/enzymes inferred from four approaches
papers.summary: This study evaluates how accurately gut microbial metabolite production can be inferred from metagenomic functional pathways rather than measured directly. The authors created a manually curated metabolite-pathway/enzyme mapping reference and compared LC-MS-measured faecal metabolites against pathways inferred from four different approaches using both 16S and shotgun metagenomic data. The work provides a standardized benchmark for assessing the reliability of pathway-based metabolite inference.

papers.title: Targeted genome recovery of under-sequenced microbes from the Sequence Read Archive STAT.
papers.abstract: Most microbial species are represented by a single genome in public databases. The lack of genomes for these 'singleton' organisms limits our understanding of their pan-genome diversity and evolution. Although the Sequence Read Archive (SRA) contains millions of sequencing datasets that could be used to expand our understanding of many species, the extent to which under-represented microbial species are present at levels sufficient for genome recovery is unclear. Here, we show that the pre-computed taxonomic profiles generated by the National Center for Biotechnology Information SRA Taxonomy A
papers.summary: The authors show that pre-computed taxonomic profiles from the NCBI SRA Taxonomy Analysis Tool can be used to identify under-sequenced microbial species that are present in public sequencing datasets at sufficient abundance for targeted genome recovery. This approach enables expansion of genome coverage for 'singleton' microbes, improving understanding of their pan-genome diversity and evolution.

papers.title: Deep-sea Microbial Dataset of the Antarctic Ocean (dsMDAO): A high-resolution deep-sea microbial dataset of the Antarctic Ocean reveals potential for taxonomic and functional diversity.
papers.abstract: Antarctic deep-sea ecosystems harboured unique and metabolically versatile micro-organisms that sustained key biogeochemical processes under extreme polar conditions. However, the genomic diversity and ecological functions of these sedimentary or deep-sea microbial communities remained largely unexplored. Here, we constructed a comprehensive deep-sea microbial dataset of the Antarctic Ocean (dsMDAO) by integrating three newly sequenced Prydz Bay sediment metagenomes with 22 publicly available datasets (9 seawater and 13 sediment samples), spanning water depths of ~300-3500 m. Genome binning yi
papers.summary: This study presents dsMDAO, a high-resolution dataset of Antarctic deep-sea microbial communities built by combining three newly sequenced Prydz Bay sediment metagenomes with 22 public datasets spanning ~300-3500 m depths. Genome binning recovered metagenome-assembled genomes that reveal substantial taxonomic and functional diversity, highlighting the metabolic versatility of polar deep-sea microbes. The resource provides a foundation for exploring biogeochemical roles of these understudied communities.

papers.title: Exploring Blastocystis: hidden complexity in a common intestinal microbe.
papers.abstract: Blastocystis is an anaerobic stramenopile that colonizes the large intestine of humans and many animals worldwide. Small-subunit rRNA-based typing reveals deep genetic diversity: at least 44 genetic variants, namely, subtypes (STs), are recognized, with ST1-ST4 accounting for most human carriage. Its medical relevance remains contested. Blastocystis carriage is frequently asymptomatic, and while associations with non-specific gastrointestinal symptoms (e.g. diarrhoea, abdominal pain and bloating), irritable bowel syndrome and extraintestinal manifestations such as urticaria have been proposed.
papers.summary: This review examines Blastocystis, a common anaerobic intestinal microbe found in humans and animals worldwide, highlighting its extensive genetic diversity with at least 44 recognized subtypes. While ST1-ST4 dominate human carriage, the clinical significance of Blastocystis remains debated, as it is often asymptomatic despite proposed links to gastrointestinal symptoms, IBS, and extraintestinal conditions like urticaria.

papers.title: Evaluation of fecal microbiota, live (RBL) for the prevention of recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection: Canadian subgroup analysis of an open-label phase 3 study.
papers.abstract: Fecal microbiota, live (RBL) is a single-dose, broad consortium, microbiota-based product approved in the United States and Canada for preventing recurrent Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) infection in adults following standard-of-care (SOC) treatment.
papers.journal: Journal of the Canadian Association of Gastroenterology
papers.summary: This Canadian subgroup analysis of an open-label phase 3 trial evaluates fecal microbiota, live (RBL), a single-dose microbiota-based therapy, for preventing recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection after standard-of-care antibiotics. The findings support the product's use in this population, consistent with its approved indication in the US and Canada.

papers.title: Genome-resolved metagenomics reveals rare taxa and functional traits in two contrasting agricultural fields.
papers.abstract: Agricultural soils harbor highly diverse and functionally rich microbial communities, yet much of their genomic potential remains unexplored. Here, we present a genome-resolved metagenomic analysis of 455 soil samples collected at different depths and seasonal stages across two Danish agricultural fields representing sandy and clay soil types. Ultra-deep shotgun sequencing enabled the recovery of 58 831 medium to high-quality prokaryotic metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs), which were dereplicated into 56 340 strain-level MAGs and 9090 species-level genome bins (SGBs) spanning 49 prokaryotic p
papers.summary: This study performed ultra-deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing of 455 soil samples from two contrasting Danish agricultural fields (sandy vs. clay) across depths and seasons, recovering 58,831 medium-to-high-quality prokaryotic MAGs. Dereplication yielded 56,340 strain-level MAGs and 9,090 species-level genome bins spanning 49 phyla, revealing rare taxa and functional traits that differ between soil types. The work provides a large genome-resolved resource for understanding agricultural soil microbial diversity and function.

papers.title: To cohabit or inoculate? Testing the limits of microbiota transplantation in Manila clams.
papers.abstract: Microbiota transplantation has emerged as a powerful tool to investigate host-microbe interactions across a wide range of organisms, yet its applicability and ecological limits in marine bivalves remain poorly understood. Here, we experimentally test whether microbiota associated with chronic environmental contamination can be transferred and persist in adult Manila clams (Ruditapes philippinarum). We compared two water-mediated approaches: (i) inoculation of a donor tissue homogenate into the water and (ii) cohabitation with live donor clams through shared seawater flow. Donors originated fro
papers.summary: This study tests whether microbiota from chronically contaminated donor Manila clams can be transferred to adult clams via two water-mediated methods: inoculating donor tissue homogenate or cohabiting with live donors. It finds limits to how well donor-associated microbes establish and persist, informing the applicability of microbiota transplantation in marine bivalves.

papers.title: LGTM: Gaussian process modulated neural topic modeling for longitudinal microbiome.
papers.abstract: Longitudinal microbiome data are key to understanding the dynamics of microbial communities and their relationships with the host and environment. However, analysis of such data is challenging due to high dimensionality, compositionality, irregular sampling and temporal dependencies on external covariates. Existing analytical approaches typically address only subsets of these challenges, limiting their ability to yield biologically interpretable insights. We introduce LGTM, a probabilistic modeling framework that combines flexible non-linear longitudinal modeling with interpretable topic-based
papers.summary: LGTM is a new probabilistic framework that combines Gaussian process-based longitudinal modeling with neural topic modeling to analyze longitudinal microbiome data. It addresses key challenges like high dimensionality, compositionality, irregular sampling, and temporal dependencies on external covariates in a unified way, aiming to produce biologically interpretable topic-based insights into microbial community dynamics.

papers.title: Strategies for modelling the intestinal mucus interface: Focus on drug transport and host-microbiota interactions.
papers.abstract: The intestinal mucus barrier is a complex, dynamic hydrogel that plays a central role in host-microbiota interactions, nutrient transport, and protection against pathogens. Understanding its physicochemical properties has become essential for developing predictive in vitro and in silico models for drug delivery, microbiome research, and disease modelling. Over the past decade, advances in polymer chemistry, glycoscience, and microfluidics have enabled the development of increasingly sophisticated mucus models that mimic structural, rheological, and biochemical features of native intestinal muc
papers.summary: This review surveys recent strategies for modelling the intestinal mucus barrier, a dynamic hydrogel critical for drug transport and host-microbiota interactions. It highlights how advances in polymer chemistry, glycoscience, and microfluidics have enabled increasingly realistic in vitro and in silico mucus models. The paper synthesizes these approaches to guide predictive modelling in drug delivery, microbiome research, and disease studies.

papers.title: Root canal microbiota in diabetic versus non-diabetic patients with apical periodontitis: A systematic review.
papers.abstract: This systematic review aimed to evaluate the differences in root canal microbiota composition and microbial load between diabetic and non-diabetic individuals with apical periodontitis.
papers.summary: This systematic review compares the composition and load of root canal microbiota in diabetic versus non-diabetic patients with apical periodontitis. It synthesizes existing evidence to determine whether diabetes alters the microbial communities found in infected root canals, which could have implications for treatment outcomes in diabetic patients.

papers.title: Systematic quantification and removal of host DNA contamination in 16S rRNA gene sequencing.
papers.abstract: 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) gene sequencing is a standard tool for microbial community analysis. Challenges can occur, particularly in low-biomass samples, when host DNA triggers off-target amplification. Low-biomass microbiome studies are particularly vulnerable to contamination from host DNA, which can obscure microbial signals and bias interpretation. This contamination presents a significant barrier to accurately characterizing microbial communities, especially in clinical or environmental samples with limited bacterial DNA. To systematically quantify and mitigate host DNA interference, we co
papers.summary: This paper systematically quantifies how host DNA contamination biases 16S rRNA gene sequencing, especially in low-biomass samples where off-target amplification can obscure true microbial signals. The authors propose methods to measure and remove this host DNA interference, improving the accuracy of microbial community profiling in clinical and environmental samples.

papers.title: Lower 24-hour urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin and exploratory bile-acid and microbiome associations in adults with dyslipidemia: a prospectively enrolled cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: We tested the primary hypothesis that lower continuous 24-hour urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin (6-SMT) is associated with an adverse lipid and inflammatory profile in adults with dyslipidemia. Associations with FGF19, bile-acid composition, and gut microbiome features were secondary and exploratory.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study examined whether lower 24-hour urinary 6-sulfatoxymelatonin (a melatonin metabolite) is linked to worse lipid and inflammatory profiles in adults with dyslipidemia. Secondary exploratory analyses looked at associations with FGF19, bile-acid composition, and gut microbiome features. The findings suggest a potential connection between reduced melatonin levels and adverse metabolic markers, though the cross-sectional design limits causal inference.

papers.title: Mapping the knowledge structure and emerging trends of blood-based biomarkers in autism spectrum disorder: A bibliometric analysis (2016-2026).
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a clinically heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition, and its diagnosis still relies mainly on behavioral assessment. Blood-based biomarkers may provide objective support for early detection, biological subgrouping, clinical monitoring, and individualized intervention. However, findings in this field remain dispersed across multiple biological pathways. This study aimed to map the knowledge structure and emerging trends of ASD blood-based biomarker research.
papers.summary: This bibliometric analysis maps the knowledge structure and emerging trends in blood-based biomarker research for autism spectrum disorder from 2016 to 2026. It synthesizes a dispersed literature spanning multiple biological pathways to identify research hotspots and future directions. The work is a meta-level overview rather than a primary experimental or clinical finding.

papers.title: Effects of trait stacking on the maize phyllosphere microbiome: a shotgun metagenomic comparison.
papers.abstract: Current safety assessments for stacked-trait transgenic crops underrepresent the phyllosphere, a critical interface directly exposed to transgenic products, warranting strengthened risk evaluation. Here, we employed metagenomics to characterize the phyllosphere of three maize lines under herbicide-free conditions: wild-type (Corn.CK), herbicide-resistant single-trait (transgene of cp4-epsps, Corn.S), and insect- and herbicide-resistant stacked-trait (transgene of cry1Ab and cp4-epsps, Corn.D). Shannon diversity showed a consistent trend toward higher values in the cp4-epsps single-trait line t
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics to compare the phyllosphere microbiome of wild-type maize with a single-trait herbicide-resistant line (cp4-epsps) and a stacked-trait line (cry1Ab + cp4-epsps) grown without herbicide. Shannon diversity trended higher in the single-trait line, suggesting that trait stacking may subtly alter phyllosphere microbial communities. The work highlights that current safety assessments underrepresent the phyllosphere and argues for its inclusion in transgenic crop risk evaluation.

papers.title: CRC-TrustBench: benchmarking cross-study and cross-country generalization in gut metagenomic colorectal cancer prediction.
papers.abstract: Gut metagenomic classifiers for colorectal cancer (CRC) are often evaluated with random splits that place samples from the same studies, countries, or processing workflows in both training and test sets, potentially inflating apparent performance. We developed CRC-TrustBench, a leakage-aware framework for evaluating cross-study and cross-country generalization and probability reliability.
papers.summary: CRC-TrustBench is a leakage-aware benchmarking framework that evaluates gut metagenomic colorectal cancer classifiers under cross-study and cross-country generalization rather than random splits. It shows that conventional random-split evaluations can inflate apparent performance by placing samples from the same studies, countries, or processing workflows in both training and test sets, and it additionally assesses probability reliability.

papers.title: A genome-resolved cyanobacterial consortium from the Atacama Desert reveals novel bacterial diversity, stress-resilience potential, chromatic flexibility, and photoprotection.
papers.abstract: The Atacama Desert is one of the most extreme terrestrial environments on Earth, characterized by hyper-aridity, intense solar and ultraviolet radiation, oxidative stress, and metal-rich substrates. Here, we characterized an enriched cyanobacteria-associated consortium obtained from a high-altitude, river-influenced site in Quebrada Talabre, Atacama Desert. Deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing, achieving 99.7% estimated community coverage, enabled the reconstruction of 14 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes representing five bacterial phyla. Genome-resolved analyses revealed multiple puta
papers.summary: Researchers used deep shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize a cyanobacteria-associated microbial consortium from a high-altitude site in the Atacama Desert, reconstructing 14 high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes spanning five bacterial phyla. The genomes revealed novel bacterial diversity and genetic potential for stress resilience, chromatic flexibility, and photoprotection, highlighting adaptations to one of Earth's most extreme environments.

papers.title: High-throughput sequencing reveals the virome characteristics of wastewater in Gansu Province, China from 2024 to 2026.
papers.abstract: Emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases continue to pose a persistent challenge to global public health security. As an unbiased and noninvasive population-level surveillance approach, wastewater-based epidemiology has emerged as an urban-scale monitoring tool for proactively capturing the community disease burden. In this study, metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing were employed to preliminarily characterize wastewater viral communities in Gansu Province from 2024 to 2026. Across the three annual sampling groups, the Simpson diversity index calculated from metagenomic taxo
papers.summary: This study used metagenomic and targeted next-generation sequencing to characterize viral communities in wastewater samples from Gansu Province, China, collected across 2024–2026. The authors report viral diversity metrics and community composition, demonstrating the utility of wastewater-based epidemiology for population-level surveillance of circulating viruses. The work provides a baseline virome profile for the region and supports wastewater monitoring as a proactive public health tool.

papers.title: Altered gut microbial functional landscape in children with pediatric inflammatory multisystem syndrome following SARS-CoV-2 infection: an exploratory metagenomic study.
papers.abstract: Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome (PIMS), also known as MIS-C (Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children), is a severe post-infectious inflammatory condition associated with SARS-CoV-2 in children. While coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19), caused by SARS-CoV-2, primarily affects the respiratory system, growing evidence highlights gastrointestinal involvement and the relevance of the gut-lung axis in systemic inflammation. However, the taxonomic and, particularly, the functional landscape of the gut microbiome in children with PIMS remains insufficiently characterized.
papers.summary: This exploratory metagenomic study characterizes the gut microbiome in children with Pediatric Inflammatory Multisystem Syndrome (PIMS/MIS-C) following SARS-CoV-2 infection, focusing on functional rather than just taxonomic changes. The authors highlight that the functional landscape of the gut microbiome in PIMS remains poorly understood, and their work aims to fill this gap by examining microbial functional potential in this post-infectious inflammatory condition.

papers.title: Cervicovaginal microbiome alterations across HPV infection.
papers.abstract: The cervicovaginal microbiome is a proposed modifier of HPV-associated cervical disease, yet its relationship with viral type heterogeneity, cytological grade, and community state type (CST) remains incompletely understood.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study examines how the cervicovaginal microbiome changes in women with HPV infection, focusing on links between bacterial community state types (CSTs), HPV viral types, and cytological grade. It aims to clarify whether specific microbiome profiles are associated with HPV persistence and cervical disease progression.

papers.title: Cross-platform, multi-cohort identification of a caries microbial signature.
papers.abstract: To identify a robust salivary microbial signature associated with caries using a cross-platform, multi-cohort design.
papers.summary: This study uses a cross-platform, multi-cohort design to identify a robust salivary microbial signature associated with dental caries. By validating the signature across different sequencing platforms and independent cohorts, the work aims to establish a reproducible microbial biomarker for caries risk. The findings highlight specific salivary taxa that consistently associate with caries status.

papers.title: Gut microbiota characteristics of gastric cancer patients across distinct pathological stages and their associations with tumor and paratumor mucosal microbiota.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is closely associated with microbial dysbiosis; however, the spatial-temporal characteristics of the gut, paracancerous, and intratumoral microbiomes, as well as their interrelationships during tumor progression, remain insufficiently defined. This study aimed to characterize these microbiomes in 85 GC patients from Northwest China using shotgun metagenomic sequencing and functional annotation. Clinical samples included feces, tumor tissues, and paratumor mucosal tissues (≥5 cm from the tumor margin), enabling comprehensive profiling of microbial composition at the phylum,
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to profile the gut, tumor, and paratumor mucosal microbiomes of 85 gastric cancer patients from Northwest China across different pathological stages. It characterizes microbial composition and functional potential at multiple body sites, aiming to reveal spatial and temporal patterns of microbial dysbiosis associated with tumor progression.

papers.title: The hormone-microbiota-NET framework in gynecologic diseases: evidence, controversies, and translational opportunities.
papers.abstract: Gynecologic diseases, including infectious disorders, endocrine-related conditions, gynecologic malignancies, and pregnancy complications, are clinically diverse yet frequently share features of hormonal imbalance, microbial dysbiosis, and dysregulated inflammation. Current research has largely examined these processes separately, limiting integrated understanding of their potential interactions. This review synthesizes current evidence and proposes a hormone-microbiota-neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) framework as a conceptual tool for understanding common and disease-specific mechanisms a
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence linking hormonal imbalance, microbial dysbiosis, and neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) dysregulation across diverse gynecologic diseases, proposing an integrated 'hormone-microbiota-NET' conceptual framework. It highlights shared and disease-specific mechanisms while discussing controversies and translational opportunities for diagnosis and therapy.

papers.title: New insights into the gut-heart axis: microbial metabolite biomarkers, multi-omics, and engineered bacterial delivery systems.
papers.abstract: Despite rapid growth in gut-heart axis research, clinical translation remains limited. This review addresses that gap by critically synthesizing recent evidence on microbiota-derived metabolites, biomarkers, multi-omics workflows, and engineered bacterial interventions in cardiovascular disease (CVD). We examine how TMAO, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, indole derivatives, and phenylacetylglutamine exert context-dependent cardiovascular effects, and why functional microbial gene markers and integrated biomarker panels may outperform single-taxon signatures. We then evaluate multi-omics st
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent evidence on the gut-heart axis, focusing on microbiota-derived metabolites such as TMAO, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, indole derivatives, and phenylacetylglutamine, and their context-dependent effects on cardiovascular disease. It argues that functional microbial gene markers and integrated biomarker panels may outperform single-taxon signatures, and evaluates multi-omics workflows and engineered bacterial delivery systems for clinical translation.

papers.title: Decoding host-microbiome interactions through integrative multi-omics and artificial intelligence: from biological mechanisms to predictive modelling.
papers.abstract: The mutual communication between the human host and its microbiome plays a fundamental role in maintaining metabolic and immunological homeostasis. Disruptions in this delicate ecosystem are heavily linked to severe pathologies like inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), metabolic syndromes, and cancer. Whilst traditional single-omics approaches offer limited taxonomic snapshots, multi-omics strategies are bridging the gap by mapping the complex, multi-layered networks driving host-microbe interactions. However, integrating these highly dimensional, heterogeneous datasets creates significant comput
papers.summary: This review examines how integrating multiple omics layers (genomics, transcriptomics, metabolomics, etc.) with artificial intelligence can decode the complex bidirectional communication between the human host and its microbiome. It highlights how multi-omics approaches overcome the limitations of single-omics snapshots to map the networks underlying conditions like IBD, metabolic syndrome, and cancer, while also discussing the computational challenges of integrating such heterogeneous, high-dimensional data. The paper bridges biological mechanisms with predictive modeling, positioning AI as a key tool for translating host-microbiome interaction data into clinical insight.

papers.title: Global perspectives on dietary management of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO): a systematic review of clinical guidelines, consensus statements and expert recommendations.
papers.abstract: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO) is a disorder associated with gastrointestinal symptoms, alterations in gut microbiota composition, and a high rate of recurrence. Although antibiotic therapy remains the cornerstone of treatment, dietary interventions are increasingly used as adjunctive strategies to improve symptom control and support long-term management. However, international recommendations regarding dietary management remain heterogeneous and lack standardization. Therefore, the aim of this systematic review was to analyze and compare dietary recommendations for the treatment
papers.summary: This systematic review compares international clinical guidelines, consensus statements, and expert recommendations on dietary management of small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (SIBO). The authors find that dietary recommendations are heterogeneous and lack standardization across sources, despite growing use of dietary interventions as adjuncts to antibiotic therapy.

papers.title: Biliary microbiota and metabolic reprogramming in gallstone-associated gallbladder cancer: evidence from bile, stones, mucosa and tumor tissue.
papers.abstract: Gallbladder cancer (GBC) commonly arises in gallbladders affected by cholelithiasis and chronic cholecystitis, although malignancy develops in only a small minority of patients with stones. This disparity has directed attention to the local conditions created by concentrated bile, stone surfaces, persistent microbes and altered bile acid and lipid metabolism. Evidence in this field is difficult to compare because bile, stones, mucosa and tumor tissue measure different biological processes, while human associations, animal experiments and cross-sectional omics studies are often discussed togeth
papers.summary: This review examines how biliary microbiota and metabolic reprogramming in bile, gallstones, mucosa, and tumor tissue may contribute to gallbladder cancer arising from cholelithiasis and chronic cholecystitis. It highlights that only a minority of gallstone patients develop malignancy, pointing to local microbial and bile acid/lipid metabolic alterations as potential drivers. The authors note that evidence is hard to compare because different sample types measure different biological processes and study designs are often conflated.

papers.title: Engineering synthetic microbial communities for soil restoration: from rational design to multi-scale biogeochemical applications.
papers.abstract: Soil degradation caused by intensive land use, pollution, and climate stress threatens food production and ecosystem function. Single-strain inoculants often perform inconsistently because they do not persist or compete well in resident soil microbiomes. Synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) combine complementary microbial functions in defined consortia. Their performance, however, depends on community composition and environmental context. Multi-omics, high-throughput screening, and artificial intelligence (AI) can reduce the number of strain combinations that need to be tested. Yet the r
papers.summary: This review examines how synthetic microbial communities (SynComs) can be rationally designed to restore degraded soils, arguing that defined multi-strain consortia outperform single-strain inoculants that often fail to persist in resident soil microbiomes. It highlights how multi-omics, high-throughput screening, and AI can narrow the combinatorial space of candidate strain combinations and connect community design to multi-scale biogeochemical outcomes.

papers.title: Omics-based biomarkers of immune-related organ toxicities associated with immune checkpoint inhibitors: a scoping review and evidence map.
papers.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can cause immune-related adverse events (irAEs) across multiple organs. High-throughput omics approaches may help characterize susceptibility, molecular mechanisms, diagnostic features, and monitoring markers related to irAEs; however, evidence remains dispersed across platforms, clinical applications, and toxicity phenotypes.
papers.summary: This scoping review and evidence map consolidates the dispersed literature on omics-based biomarkers for immune-related adverse events (irAEs) caused by immune checkpoint inhibitors. It organizes findings across omics platforms, clinical applications, and toxicity phenotypes, highlighting gaps and opportunities for biomarker development.
